title.en: Tale 3 — The Pot That Gave Birth

book_meta.author: traditional
book_meta.status: public domain — folk material, no known author

source: retold in modern Hebrew by Claude — NOT native-validated

sentences.en: Juha asked for a big pot from the neighbour.
The neighbour gave it to him gladly.
After two days Juha returned it.
Inside the pot was a small pot.

sentences.ar: השכן שאל: מה זה הדבר הזה?
sentences.en: The neighbour asked: what is this thing?

sentences.ar: ג'וחא אמר: הסיר שלך ילד בלילה.
sentences.en: Juha said: your pot gave birth at night.

sentences.ar: השכן צחק אבל לקח את שניהם.
sentences.en: The neighbour laughed but took both of them.

sentences.ar: הוא אמר לעצמו: זה איש טיפש.
sentences.en: He said to himself: this is a foolish man.
After a week Juha came again.
He asked for the big pot.
The neighbour gave it to him at once.
He thought about the small pot.
Two weeks passed, and then a month.
Juha did not come and did not return it.
The neighbour went to him and knocked at the door.
He asked: where is my pot?

sentences.ar: ג'וחא אמר: יש לי חדשות רעות.
sentences.en: Juha said: I have bad news.

sentences.ar: הוא אמר: הסיר שלך מת אתמול.
sentences.en: He said: your pot died yesterday.

sentences.ar: השכן צעק: סיר לא יכול למות!
sentences.en: The neighbour shouted: a pot cannot die!

sentences.ar: ג'וחא אמר: אבל הוא ילד, נכון?
sentences.en: Juha said: but it gave birth, right?

sentences.ar: הוא אמר: מי שיולד גם מת.
sentences.en: He said: whoever gives birth also dies.
